title: docs: the sample `os validate` transcript on validating-metadata.mdx prints a stale author-time rule count (38 shown, registry holds more)
body:
Filed unassigned while auditing the "one gate, four doors" table for #9007 (PR #9033). ⛔ No `domain:*` set — triage's single-producer field. Deliberately **not** fixed in that PR: its card forbids writing a hard count anywhere on the page, and any number typed here is the same defect one release later, so the fix carries a decision that is triage's to make.

## Measured

`content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, the clean-run sample under `## The one gate, four doors`:

```
  → Running author-time rules (38)...
```

`AUTHORING_RULES` in `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` holds more entries than that today, and **every** entry lists `validate` in its `commands` (the three data-model entries are `['validate', 'build']`; all others are all three), so `authoringRulesFor('validate').length` — the number the CLI prints — is the whole registry. The transcript therefore understates what a real run reports.

This is the same drift class as #7491 ("two code comments still say 26 shared AUTHORING_RULES"), which was closed by refreshing the number. That is one of the two options below, and it is the one that will need doing again.

## The decision

- **A. Refresh the number.** One-line edit, matches #7491's precedent, and stale again the next time a rule lands — the registry has gained entries steadily since #4463.
- **B. Elide the count from the sample.** e.g. `→ Running author-time rules...`, which is what the surrounding page settled on after PR #9005 removed a false rule count from the table's footnote rather than replacing it with another one, and pointed readers at each rule's own entry in `AUTHORING_RULES` as the authority. The cost is that the sample no longer shows the CLI's real output verbatim.
- **C. B plus a gate.** If the number is worth keeping, something has to hold it to the registry; nothing does today, which is why it drifted. That is a bigger change than either edit and probably not worth it for one sample transcript.

Recommendation: **B**. A perishable count inside an illustrative transcript buys the reader nothing that the registry pointer does not, and this exact page has already paid for one wrong count.

## For triage

- **Dedupe**: searched open issues for the sample-output / author-time-rule-count drift at 07:20Z — nothing open; #7491 is the closed precedent for the same class in code comments.
- **Scope**: `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` only, and only the fenced sample block — the table above it is being corrected in PR #9033, which does not touch this block.
- `content/docs/releases/**` stays out of scope as always.
